d: A banking crisis has pushed Paraguay into political turmoil. Around three million customers have been locked out of their accounts at Ueno Bank, triggering protests and raising questions about public money, political connections and accountability. President Santiago Pena, who once held shares in the bank's parent company, is now facing mounting pressure. Even his own Colorado Party has turned against him. How did a banking collapse become a political crisis? And what does it mean for Paraguay's future?
